issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds \|fg\|_{L^s} \leq \|f\|_{L^s}\|g\|_{L^1} and claims \|\mathscr{F}(\rho_\epsilon)\|_{L^1}=1. The pointwise product inequality requires \|g\|_{L^\infty}, not \|g\|_{L^1}; moreover \|\mathscr{F}(\rho_\epsilon)\|_{L^1} is not 1 (only \|\rho_\epsilon\|_{L^1}=1). The valid route is \|fg\|_{L^s}\leq\|f\|_{L^s}\|g\|_{L^\infty} with \|\mathscr{F}(\rho_\epsilon)\|_{L^\infty}\leq 1 (positive mollifier with unit mass), which yields the same conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the product inequality with \|fg\|_{L^s}\leq\|f\|_{L^s}\|g\|_{L^\infty} and replace \|\mathscr{F}(\rho_\epsilon)\|_{L^1}=1 with \|\mathscr{F}(\rho_\epsilon)\|_{L^\infty}\leq 1.
issues.overall_effect: One proof step in Proposition prop:SobolevModulation_embedding uses an invalid inequality and a false equality; the proposition's conclusion is nonetheless recoverable with a corrected one-line argument.
issues.title: Wrong norm used in mollifier Fourier estimate
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction (L^1 to L^\infty) preserves the conclusion with no change to any claim, rate, or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The thesis follows by observing that, for every $x,y\in\Omega$, we can write \[|x+y|=2|(x+y)/2|=2|z|\] where $z=(x+y)/2\in\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: For convex Ω, the set identity Ω+Ω=2Ω is correct, but the Lebesgue measure scales as |2Ω| = 2^d |Ω|, not 2|Ω|. The proof confuses the pointwise norm identity |x+y| = 2|z| with the measure scaling, concluding the factor 2 instead of 2^d. The correct constant is 2^{d/p}|Ω|^{1/p}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2^{1/p} with 2^{d/p} in the corollary's bound (and propagate the corrected constant to downstream convex-case estimates).
issues.overall_effect: The constant 2^{1/p} in the convex-domain embedding bound is wrong for d>1; downstream convex-case bounds in Proposition prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local and Corollary cor:Barron inherit the wrong constant.
issues.title: Convex-domain improvement constant wrong in dimension d>1
issues.why_classification: The conclusion (embedding with a domain-dependent constant) survives but the stated constant is quantitatively wrong for d>1; fixing it requires propagating a corrected factor through dependent results but no new lemma or proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof is a combination of \cref{thm:approximation_sobolev_space_local} and \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space} as well as \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space_convex}.

Additionally, the lemma bounds ‖χ_Ωf‖ but the theorem requires ‖f‖_{M^{p,q}_m}, and the step ‖χ_Ωf‖_{FL^q} ≤ ‖f‖_{FL^q} is not valid in general. For p>1 the theorem requires s_1 > d/p' but the proposition's hypothesis has s_1 = 0.

f(x) = C_{\sigma ,\varphi}\int_{\rr{2d}}\int_{\rr{}} \rho(x, y, \eta, b) \, e^{-2\pi ib\cdot \tau} \, V_\phi{f}(y, \eta) \,db\,dy\,d\eta

issues.failure_explanation: The STFT representation of f integrates y over all of ℝ^d, but the dictionary D̃_Ω only contains atoms with spatial shifts y ∈ Ω. The measure μ_f(y,η,b) is not supported on Ω×ℝ^d×ℝ (since V_φf(y,η) ≠ 0 for y ∉ Ω), so f = ∫_{D̃_Ω} dμ_f is false. Consequently f need not lie in the variation space K(D̃_Ω), and Maurey's theorem cannot be applied. A Gaussian f centered far from Ω gives ‖f‖_{M^{p,q}_m} finite but atoms in D̃_Ω exponentially small at f's support, so the infimum error cannot vanish as N→∞.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: M^{p_1,q_1}_{v_{t_1}\otimes v_{s_1}}(\rr d) \hookrightarrow M^{p_2,q_2}_{v_{t_2}\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr d)

issues.failure_explanation: The global proof's weight θ(η,b) = v_{n+s}(η)/v_s(b) requires s > 1 (for ∫v_{-s}(b)db < ∞), so the variation norm involves M^1_{1⊗v_{n+s}} with n+s > n+1. Applying Theorem thm:embeddings to embed M^{p,q}_{v_{s_1}⊗v_{s_2}} into M^1_{1⊗v_{n+s}} with (C1) requires s_2 ≥ n+s > n+1, but eq:indices gives s_2 = n+1 for q ≤ 1. Condition (C2) requires q > 1 and is inapplicable. The proof's claim that 'the arguments work for any s>1, extending the range to eq:indices' fails for q ≤ 1.

failure_location.quote: The arguments above work for any index $s>1$, this allows to extend the range of $s_2$ as in \eqref{eq:indices}, providing to choose $s>1$ accordingly.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the weight condition to s_2 > n+1 (strict inequality) for 0 < q ≤ 1 in eq:indices as used in Theorem thm:approximation_sobolev_space_G and propagate to cor:added-2 and cor:added-3.
issues.overall_effect: For 0 < q ≤ 1 the embedding needed in the global theorem's proof does not hold under the stated weight conditions s_2 = n+1; the theorem and its corollaries are unproved in this parameter range.
issues.title: Global theorem weight condition s_2 = n+1 insufficient for q ≤ 1
issues.why_classification: The N^{-1/2} rate and the qualitative conclusion survive with a slightly stronger weight condition (s_2 > n+1 instead of s_2 = n+1); no new proof architecture is needed, but the stated admissible range is weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the triangle inequality, $|V_\varphi \sigma(x,\omega)| \geq |T_2(x,\omega)| - |T_1(x,\omega)| = \frac{1}{2\pi}e^{-\pi x^2} - |T_1(x,\omega)|$. This implies the lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound}.

issues.failure_explanation: At (x,ω) = (0,0) Lemma lem:relu-origin gives |V_φσ(0,0)| = 1/(2π) = (1/(2π))e^0, so the strict inequality fails with equality. The proof's triangle-inequality step yields |V| ≥ (1/(2π))e^{-πx²} − |T_1|, which does not imply |V| > (1/(2π))e^{-πx²} (that would require |T_1| < 0). The identity-theorem argument for non-vanishing is also invalid (a holomorphic function on ℂ² can have zeros on ℝ² without vanishing identically).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the strict inequality with a non-strict one (or a weaker lower bound), and replace the identity-theorem argument with a real-analyticity/zero-set-measure argument to prove non-vanishing.
issues.overall_effect: The strict lower bound in Corollary cor:31 is false at the origin and the proof of non-vanishing is invalid; however, the non-vanishing claim can be established by real-analyticity of V_φσ, and Condition (A) is unaffected since it only needs non-vanishing at some (t,τ) with τ ≠ 0.
issues.title: Strict lower bound for STFT of ReLU is false at the origin
issues.why_classification: The false strict bound can be weakened locally and the non-vanishing claim (the only input needed for Condition (A)) survives with a standard real-analyticity argument; no downstream guarantee is lost.
